# std/display.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/display.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Windows, a frame buffer and input events, for programs
on the hosted target, over the `host_display` builtin. On Linux and the
BSDs (64-bit) this is X11, loaded at run time with dlopen, so a program
needs no X library to build and gets a failure (`None`, `false`) where
there is no display or no libX11. Windows and macOS report failure for now.
`host_display` is stage1 only and needs the C backend:
backend: c

`import "std/display.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [std/host.bastio](std-host.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`dsp_open`](#dsp_open) | Opens a window `w` by `h` pixels (each 1 to 16384) with a title and shows it. |
| [`dsp_close`](#dsp_close) | Closes a window. |
| [`dsp_present`](#dsp_present) | Draws `pixels` (`w * h * 3` bytes, red green blue, rows from the top; or `w * h * 4` with an alpha byte that is ignored) at the window's top left corner. |
| [`dsp_size`](#dsp_size) | The window's current size (it changes when the user resizes it, see `EV_RESIZE`). |
| [`dsp_screen`](#dsp_screen) | The screen's size. |
| [`dsp_title`](#dsp_title) | Sets the window's title. |
| [`dsp_next`](#dsp_next) | The next event for any of the program's windows, waiting at most `ms` milliseconds (`DSP_FAIL`. |
| [`dsp_fd`](#dsp_fd) | The descriptor of the connection to the display, to wait on with `poll` or epoll (`std/os.bastio`) together with other descriptors; when it is readable `dsp_next(host, 0)` has an event. |
| [`dsp_errno`](#dsp_errno) | The error number (`errno`) of the last call of this module that failed (ENODEV. |
| [`dsp_word`](#dsp_word) | Little-endian word `i` of an event record (what `dsp_next` unpacks). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `DSP_FAIL`

```bastio
const DSP_FAIL: u64 = 18446744073709551615;
```

### `EV_NONE`

```bastio
const EV_NONE: u64 = 0;
```

What `dsp_next` returns, in `Event::kind`: 0 nothing before the time limit.

### `EV_CLOSE`

```bastio
const EV_CLOSE: u64 = 1;
```

The window manager asked to close the window (`a`, `b`, `c` unused).

### `EV_KEY_DOWN`

```bastio
const EV_KEY_DOWN: u64 = 2;
```

A key went down: `a` its X keysym (Latin-1 characters are their codes, Return 65293, Escape 65307, Left 65361, ...), `b` the modifier mask (1 shift, 2 caps lock, 4 control, 8 alt), `c` the key code.

### `EV_KEY_UP`

```bastio
const EV_KEY_UP: u64 = 3;
```

A key went up (fields as for `EV_KEY_DOWN`).

### `EV_MOUSE_MOVE`

```bastio
const EV_MOUSE_MOVE: u64 = 4;
```

The pointer moved: `a`, `b` the position in the window (signed), `c` the button and modifier mask.

### `EV_MOUSE_DOWN`

```bastio
const EV_MOUSE_DOWN: u64 = 5;
```

A button went down: `a`, `b` the position, `c` the button (1 left, 2 middle, 3 right).

### `EV_MOUSE_UP`

```bastio
const EV_MOUSE_UP: u64 = 6;
```

A button went up (fields as for `EV_MOUSE_DOWN`).

### `EV_WHEEL`

```bastio
const EV_WHEEL: u64 = 7;
```

The wheel turned: `a`, `b` the position, `c` 1 for up and 2^64 - 1 for down.

### `EV_RESIZE`

```bastio
const EV_RESIZE: u64 = 8;
```

The window changed size: `a` the new width, `b` the new height (`dsp_size` gives the same).

### `EV_EXPOSE`

```bastio
const EV_EXPOSE: u64 = 9;
```

Part of the window needs painting again: call `dsp_present`.

### `EV_TEXT`

```bastio
const EV_TEXT: u64 = 10;
```

Text was typed: `a` the Unicode code point (follows the key down that made it; not sent while control or alt is held).

### `DspSize`

```bastio
struct DspSize { w: u64, h: u64 }
```

A width and a height in pixels.

### `Event`

```bastio
struct Event { kind: u64, window: u64, a: u64, b: u64, c: u64 }
```

One event: the kind, the window it is for and three fields whose meaning depends on the kind.

## Functions

### `dsp_open`

```bastio
fn dsp_open(h: &Host, w: u64, ht: u64, title: Str) -> Option[u64]
```

Opens a window `w` by `h` pixels (each 1 to 16384) with a title and shows it. At most 16 windows are open at once.

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_open(host, 64, 48, "demo") {
  Option::Some(win) => { dsp_close(host, win); }
  Option::None => { }   // no display here
}
```

### `dsp_close`

```bastio
fn dsp_close(h: &Host, win: u64) -> bool
```

Closes a window.

### `dsp_present`

```bastio
fn dsp_present(h: &Host, win: u64, w: u64, ht: u64, pixels: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Draws `pixels` (`w * h * 3` bytes, red green blue, rows from the top; or `w * h * 4` with an alpha byte that is ignored) at the window's top left corner. It is the whole frame: what is outside it keeps the previous picture, and what lies outside the window is cut off.

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_open(host, 2, 1, "frame") {
  Option::Some(win) => {
    let mut px = balloc(6);
    bset(&mut px, 0, 255);
    let ok = dsp_present(host, win, 2, 1, px);
    bfree(px);
    if !ok { return 1; }
    dsp_close(host, win);
  },
  Option::None => { },
}
```

### `dsp_size`

```bastio
fn dsp_size(h: &Host, win: u64) -> Option[DspSize]
```

The window's current size (it changes when the user resizes it, see `EV_RESIZE`): width and height.

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_open(host, 8, 6, "size") {
  Option::Some(win) => {
    match dsp_size(host, win) {
      Option::Some(s) => { if s.w != 8 || s.h != 6 { return 1; } },
      Option::None => { return 2; },
    }
    dsp_close(host, win);
  },
  Option::None => { },
}
```

### `dsp_screen`

```bastio
fn dsp_screen(h: &Host) -> Option[DspSize]
```

The screen's size: width and height.

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_screen(host) {
  Option::Some(s) => { if s.w == 0 || s.h == 0 { return 1; } },
  Option::None => { },   // no display here
}
```

### `dsp_title`

```bastio
fn dsp_title(h: &Host, win: u64, title: Str) -> bool
```

Sets the window's title.

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_open(host, 8, 8, "before") {
  Option::Some(win) => {
    if !dsp_title(host, win, "after") { return 1; }
    dsp_close(host, win);
  },
  Option::None => { },
}
```

### `dsp_next`

```bastio
fn dsp_next(h: &Host, ms: u64) -> Option[Event]
```

The next event for any of the program's windows, waiting at most `ms` milliseconds (`DSP_FAIL`: no limit, 0: do not wait). Kind `EV_NONE` means the time ran out; `None` means the connection to the display failed.

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_open(host, 8, 8, "events") {
  Option::Some(win) => {
    match dsp_next(host, 0) {
      Option::Some(e) => { if e.kind > EV_TEXT { return 1; } },
      Option::None => { return 2; },
    }
    dsp_close(host, win);
  },
  Option::None => { },
}
```

### `dsp_fd`

```bastio
fn dsp_fd(h: &Host) -> Option[u64]
```

The descriptor of the connection to the display, to wait on with `poll` or epoll (`std/os.bastio`) together with other descriptors; when it is readable `dsp_next(host, 0)` has an event.

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_open(host, 8, 8, "fd") {
  Option::Some(win) => {
    match dsp_fd(host) {
      Option::Some(fd) => { if fd > 1000000 { return 1; } },
      Option::None => { return 2; },
    }
    dsp_close(host, win);
  },
  Option::None => { },
}
```

### `dsp_errno`

```bastio
fn dsp_errno(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The error number (`errno`) of the last call of this module that failed (ENODEV: no display, ENOSYS: no libX11 or not supported here, ENOTSUP: the display is not 24-bit color).

Example:

```bastio
match dsp_size(host, 99999) {
  Option::Some(s) => { return 1; },
  Option::None => { },
}
if dsp_errno(host) == 0 { return 2; }
```

### `dsp_word`

```bastio
fn dsp_word(b: &Bytes, i: u64) -> u64
  requires i < 5 && blen(b) >= 40
```

Little-endian word `i` of an event record (what `dsp_next` unpacks).

Example:

```bastio
let mut rec = balloc(40);
bset(&mut rec, 8, 7);
let bad = dsp_word(rec, 1) != 7 || dsp_word(rec, 0) != 0;
bfree(rec);
if bad { return 1; }
```
